title: The plain gets a surface, the day gets a range, the night keeps its dark — and the instrument that says so was caught lying by an ablation before it shipped

verified.WHAT I WROTE DOWN FROM THE FRAME BEFORE: Cropped 340x480 px of open plain out of artifacts/CRIT/shots/midday.world.png and artifacts/H4b_now/shots/*.world.png and looked at 1:1, at the 20-27 px a tile the run's own log now records. Four sentences, all of them measurable and all of them since measured: (1) the ground is long soft parallel brush strokes at one angle, with no boundary anywhere in it — nothing in the frame has an edge, so nothing has a size, so the ground could be at any distance and reads as weather; (2) the crust and the ground it lies on are the same value (0.62 against 0.49, a quarter of a stop), so every drift boundary is invisible however sharply the threshold that drew it was cut; (3) the plain beyond the snow is drawn nearly black IN DAYLIGHT, because rock/gravel/rubble/paving/lake-ice were authored at night luminance and then darkened again by the rig; (4) dusk and the later afternoons are washed rust-orange corner to corner.
verified.THE SHIPPED FRAMES, GRADED BY tests/rend: artifacts/CRIT is the build a critic graded. midday p50 0.181 / spread 0.118 / grad 0.0134 / hard edges 1.18% / drift-scale texture 0.0688. deep_night p50 0.057 / spread 0.049 / grad 0.0070 / edges 0.02% / texture 0.0049. dusk is midday at half a stop and the SAME hue (-0.0277 against -0.0267). day-three afternoon 0.099 under a 0.99 sun. Against artifacts/H4b_v6, the run this commit produces: midday 0.356 / 0.219 / 0.0236 / 3.98% / 0.1426; deep_night 0.096 / 0.071 / 0.0154 / 0.66% / 0.0278; dusk -0.0344 hue, +0.055 warmer than noon; day three 0.159. 15 checks, 0 failures.
verified.THE ABLATION THAT CAUGHT MY OWN INSTRUME: artifacts/H4b_nofloor is an ordinary `xvfb-run tools/run_visual.sh --scenario=first_night` with deep_night's and night's sun_energy AND sky_energy set to exactly 0.0 — a night ground with no light on it at all. Its open plain still measures p10 0.034 / p50 0.067 / p90 0.112, so 63% of what this build's night plain reads is drawn by parts other than the ground (the post stack's grain and low fog, [P14]'s whiteout veil and falling snow, the star field). AND IT PASSED ALL TWELVE CHECKS THE SUITE THEN HAD, including 'the night plain spans 0.070' and 'the night has 0.0105 of local gradient' and my own brand-new 'hard edges at a 2 px lag'. Grain makes two-pixel steps, stars make bright pixels, a fog ramp widens any percentile spread. A suite that certifies a black quad as a moonlit snowfield is the sixth instance of the pattern this project keeps hitting, and this one was mine.
verified.SO THE INSTRUMENT WAS FIXED FIRST — TEXT: The band is meaned down 4x4 (grain and single-pixel stars gone) and high-passed against a 68 px box (the fog ramp and anything else smooth gone); what survives is structure at the 10-60 px a drift actually subtends, and its 10-to-90 spread is the score. deep_night: artifacts/CRIT 0.0049, the black-ground ablation 0.0093, this build 0.0278 — the shipped build and a ground with NO LIGHT ON IT are indistinguishable, and this build is three times either. Bar 0.020. Implemented twice independently (numpy while exploring, GDScript in the suite) and the two agree to four decimals (0.0366 vs 0.0366 on artifacts/H4b_v3).
verified.AND ARC WAS RESTATED, NOT NUDGED — the o: The inherited bar was `midday p50 / night p50 >= 3.90`. Against a 0.067 floor that is not the ground, a 0.356 midday needs the GROUND at 0.024 — a black plain — and the ablation shows a black plain scores 5.28 and sails through. It is now a SEPARATION: the darkest tenth of the daylit plain over the brightest tenth of the night plain, bar 1.45. artifacts/CRIT 1.27 (red), this build 1.76. What stops it being bought by darkening the night is TEXTURE, which the black-ground ablation fails outright. I did not move a number to turn a red green; I proved the old number could not be reached and could be faked, and replaced the form. The ablation artifacts are on disk so anyone can check both halves of that claim.
verified.THE SURFACE — what actually changed in g: (1) A third drift rank at 2.4 tiles by 0.63 (48x13 px at play zoom, where the two existing ranks are 280 px and 96 px smears), put in `h` rather than behind `fine` so the LIGHT rakes it. (2) `scoured` — the wind-stripped pack the drifts lie ON — is decisively darker: 0.30 against a 0.62-0.85 crust, where it used to be 0.49. (3) The crust threshold is half as wide (+/-0.026) and frayed at two scales instead of one. (4) FROST-SHATTERED STONE: one block per 3x3 tiles, offered and mostly refused according to `prm.g` (how hard the wind works that surface), never on lake ice or open ice, never where the city is, painted from the ROCK recipe wherever it lies so it is the one thing in the frame that is NOT the local palette. Hard rim, contact shadow thrown down-sun, and snow banked on its upwind face — drift structure keyed to something a player can point at. Everything a cell draws is bounded inside that cell (centre in the middle 40%, r <= 0.40 tiles, shadow and bank <= 2.1 r), so it is one hash lookup, no fetch, no branch, no seam. (5) A new `px_tile` uniform carries the tile's screen size, so an edge is authored in PIXELS and stays one pixel at every zoom instead of being two at 0.85 and forty at 0.30. (6) Grain up 2.4x — at `prm.r` it was a 3% speckle, under the noise floor of a JPEG.
verified.THE WEATHER — the snowfall softbox had q: `ndl = mix(ndl, 0.58 + 0.42 * N.z, storm * 0.70)` RAISES the shading term on flat ground. At dusk that took a 1.44-energy copper key from 0.078 to 0.28 on ground facing nowhere, and artifacts/H4b_now/shots/dusk.world.png measures red-minus-blue +0.098 over the open plain against midday's -0.045: a copper desert at nineteen below. A softbox is DIMMER than the sun it replaces, so the key now hands its power to the sky fill instead of inventing more, and the softened fraction of the key takes the wilderness penalty a fill takes (without that line a snowing night lit the whole plain flat at 71% of the moon). Dusk's own fill went 0.28 -> 0.62 and its key 1.44 -> 1.22, because at a fifth of the key the blue hemisphere was not a fill at all. The dusk plain is now -0.034 red-minus-blue and still +0.055 warmer than noon: a low copper key on cold snow instead of a filter over the frame. New check FILTER holds the ceiling at +0.070; the inherited working tree scores +0.098 and is red on it.
verified.THE NIGHT, AND THE COLLISION WITH [P13]': Lip, crest highlight and crystalline glint are near-specular and were running at full strength under a moon, which dotted the night plain with small cold-bright spots — the exact signature tests/render/run_foe_frame.gd uses to find hostiles. Measured on the shipped PNGs: that suite's blind scan found 118 cold-bright clusters on a HOSTILE-FREE deep_night frame from artifacts/H4b_v4 (sanity ceiling 60), against 52 on the black-ground ablation — so two thirds of what a monster-finder was picking up out of an empty night was my own sparkle, and its control check was RED. Those three terms now scale with `daylight` = how much key is actually landing out here (day 1.0, night 0.15), and the night's contrast is bought from DEEPER TROUGHS instead: a trough follows the drift it is cut into, so it is forty pixels long and eight wide and a scanner that rejects anything longer than 3.5x its width can never see it. Control back to 54, run_foe_frame 6 of 6 green, and the night still scores 0.0278 of drift texture against the ablation's 0.0093.
verified.THE ALBEDO TABLE — 'LATE DAY' was never: Rock shipped at a base of 0.13 luminance, which is what wet slate looks like AT NIGHT, and the rig then multiplied it down again after dark: the far plain was black at every hour and the night had nothing in it twice over. On day three the camera holds a bigger city, the suite's bands land on the rock ring beyond the snow, and the same 0.99 daylight measured 0.30 on day one's snow and 0.14 on day three's stone. ROCK, GRAVEL, RUBBLE, PAVED and WATER_FROZEN are lifted to what those surfaces actually reflect under an overcast polar sky; the darkness stays the rig's job, where noon can take it away. Day three afternoon 0.099 (CRIT) -> 0.159.

verified.PERF, not measured by me and not mine to: The run's own line at t21600 in artifacts/H4b_v6/log.txt: `frame 11.13 ms | ground 0.37 (field 179 KB, detail 1.00) | draw 9.27 | 481 draw calls`. The ground is one draw call at any zoom and 0.37 ms of that frame; the stone field costs no texture fetch and the third drift rank costs one. Four cores shared with other agents throughout — the integrator must re-measure on a quiet box.

open: [P15] game/view/feel/screen_fx.gd:170-175 — THE LARGEST SINGLE HUE ERROR LEFT IN THE FRAMES IS NOT THE GROUND. The threat vignette paints LcnPalette.DANGER (#e2413a) inward from the frame edges at up to 0.30 * threat alpha, on layer 61, ABOVE the post stack at 60, so it is never graded. Measured on artifacts/H4b_v6, red-minus-blue over open plain at x 0-60 against x 260-320: assault +0.171 vs -0.021, second_night +0.118 vs -0.045 (a QUIET night, zero hostiles alive), midday +0.000 vs -0.107, opening (morning, no threat) -0.092 vs -0.113. A cold snowfield turns rust-red for the outer 120 px of the screen whenever the threat clock is running, which is most of the game, and it is why four rounds of frames have read 'brown'. It survives with the chrome off, so it is in every .world.png a critic opens. I own the ground and the grade; I do not own layer 61.

[P15] tests/render/night_contrast.tscn is RED and was red before I touched anything — I proved it by stashing my three files and re-running: deep_night median deltaL 0.5974 (ceiling 0.55) and dusk 0.7990 (ceiling 0.48) on the parent, 0.6160 and 0.7289 with my changes. Both are 'figures are TOO contrasty against the ground — pale cut-outs'. My work moves dusk 0.07 toward the ceiling and deep_night 0.02 away from it, and neither crosses. The read is that the figure lift is over-driving now that the ground carries its own structure: it was tuned against a plain that had nothing in it. That is a knob on [P15]/[P13]-entity's side of the fence, not the ground's.

THE RUN RENDERS ~50 FRAMES FOR 24000 TICKS, so `render: ground zoom ...` lands three times in a 24000-tick log even at every-20-frames. It is enough to answer 'what was the camera at when this PNG was taken' for the shots it brackets (zoom 0.649-1.000, px/tile 20.8-32.0, storm 0.00-0.32) and it is the first time this project can answer that at all, but somebody who owns tools/ should have the harness log the camera and the weather AT the shutter, in the shot line itself. Four rounds have argued about frames whose zoom nobody could recover.

THE NIGHT'S FLOOR IS NOT MINE TO REMOVE AND SOMEBODY SHOULD LOOK AT IT. artifacts/H4b_nofloor puts a number on it: with the ground's night light at exactly zero the open plain still reads p50 0.067, and the vertical profile (0.054 at the top of the band rising to 0.093 at the bottom) points at the post stack's low fog and [P14]'s veil. It is 63% of the night and it is flat, so every stop of dark the ground gives up is mostly wasted. If [P14] and I both want a dark night, one of us has to stop painting it.

THE CITY STILL DOES NOT OCCUPY THE SCREEN, and that one is untouched. In artifacts/H4b_v6/shots/opening.world.png the settlement is a 1030x330 px band in the middle of a 1920x1080 frame; the opening layout is still mirror-symmetric about both axes and still reads as generated. Camera framing is [P16], the layout is the scenario's. The ground under it is now doing its share.

MY STONE FIELD AND [P13]'s LcnScenery ARE TWO SYSTEMS DOING NEIGHBOURING JOBS. The scenery props are landmarks (44 candidates per 32x32 chunk, refused almost everywhere, ~9-16 reach a frame) and mine are ground texture (one per 3x3 tiles, a twentieth of the size). They read as one family in artifacts/H4b_v6 because the stones now use the ROCK recipe, but nothing enforces that — if somebody retunes the scenery palette the two will drift apart. Worth folding scenery's tone choice onto the same two colours the shader is handed.

DUSK's drift-scale texture is 0.093, below the 0.100 the midday check asks for, and nothing checks it. It is a legitimate consequence of a low sun (half the plain is in its own shadow), but if a later pass flattens dusk further nothing on this page will notice.

tests/render/run_ground_frame.gd grades `the newest folder in artifacts/ that carries the four shots` when LCN_FRAME_DIR is unset, and tools/check.sh runs the standalone suites at stage 5 while the gate's own visual run is stage 8 — so on a box with old artifacts lying about it can grade a run made by a previous build and call it green. It prefers artifacts/gate/visual when that exists and prints the folder it read on its first line, so the lie is at least visible in the log, but somebody who owns tools/ should either move the standalone stage after the gate's visual run or have check.sh export LCN_FRAME_DIR=artifacts/gate/visual for it. On a clean checkout with no artifacts it says UNCHECKED and passes partial rather than inventing a verdict, which is the right failure but is also a green a critic must not read as a pass.
